headline: Record sales and cheap ECB money lift BMW
text: BMW sold a record 1,668,982 BMW, Mini and Rolls-Royce cars in 2011, and Rolls-Royce reported record sales on Asian demand. Fears about the eurozone have eased since the European Central Bank lent banks 489 billion euros for three years at 1% on 22 December, and BMW shares rose 27% in January.
source: BMW Group Annual Report 2011 (deliveries 2011), https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_2011.pdf (read 2026-10-03); The Guardian, 'Rolls-Royce hits new sales record on Asian demand', 9 January 2012 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_debt_crisis (LTRO, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The new BMW 3 Series at the Detroit motor show, January 2012

headline: Glencore and Xstrata agree a 'merger of equals'
text: After confirming talks on 2 February, Glencore and Xstrata announced on 7 February a recommended all-share merger: Xstrata holders would get 2.8 new Glencore shares each, valuing Xstrata at 1,290p a share or £39.1bn, a 15% premium. Glencore already owns 34% of Xstrata. Mick Davis would run the combined Glencore Xstrata, with Ivan Glasenberg as deputy and president; the deal needs 75% of the votes of Xstrata's independent shareholders. Completion is expected in the third quarter.
imageCaption: Ivan Glasenberg, Glencore's chief executive, at the St. Gallen Symposium

headline: Warren Buffett reveals a 10.9 billion dollar bet on IBM
text: In his annual letter Warren Buffett said Berkshire Hathaway bought 63.9 million IBM shares in 2011 for 10.9 billion dollars, 5.5% of the company. He praised Lou Gerstner and Sam Palmisano and said Berkshire should wish for a low share price while IBM buys back its own stock. Ginni Rometty became IBM's first woman chief executive in January.
imageCaption: Warren Buffett

headline: Kazuo Hirai named chief executive
text: On 1 February Sony said Kazuo Hirai, who ran the PlayStation business, will become president and chief executive on 1 April, succeeding Howard Stringer.
imageCaption: Howard Stringer (left) and Kazuo Hirai, the successor he named as Sony's chief executive
imageCredit: Getty Images (press photograph, via CBS News)

headline: Citigroup fails the Fed's stress test
text: The Federal Reserve rejected Citigroup's plan to return capital to shareholders after its annual stress test, citing the bank's planned payouts and the risks in its international loans.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citigroup (read 2026-10-03, citing CBS News, Huffington Post and MarketWatch, March 2012)
imageCaption: The Federal Reserve Board's Eccles Building, Washington

headline: Cisco to buy NDS for $5 billion
text: Cisco announced on March 15 that it will acquire NDS Group, a maker of software for pay-television operators, for $5 billion.

headline: Another warning sends Nokia to a 14-year low
text: On 11 April Nokia again said results will miss its forecasts. Its US shares fell 16% to 4.24 dollars, the lowest since February 1998. Nokia has sold about 2 million Lumia Windows phones; in the past quarter it burned about 700 million euros of cash.
imageCaption: The Nokia Lumia 800, the Windows Phone launched in late 2011

headline: Nestlé buys Pfizer's baby nutrition business
text: On 23 April Nestlé agreed to buy Pfizer's infant nutrition business, formerly Wyeth Nutrition, for $11.9 billion. It makes Nestlé much bigger in baby formula.

headline: Sony doubles its loss forecast to 520 billion yen
text: On 10 April Sony said its loss for the year to March will be 520 billion yen, about 6.4 billion dollars, more than twice its February forecast, because of write-offs of deferred tax assets. Its US shares fell 10% that day.
imageCaption: The Sony Building in the Ginza district, Tokyo

headline: New York Times: Wal-Mart hushed up bribery in Mexico
text: The New York Times reported on 21 April that Wal-Mart de Mexico paid more than 24 million dollars in bribes to win permits for new stores, and that headquarters shut down its own investigation without telling the authorities. Shares of the Mexican unit fell 12% on the Monday after the report.
source: https://abcnews.go.com/blogs/business/2012/04/wal-mart-de-mexico-engaged-in-widespread-bribery-nytimes-reports (search result summary read 2026-10-03); https://money.cnn.com/2012/04/22/news/companies/walmart-mexico-bribery/index.htm (search result summary read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Wal-Mart store in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico ;;

headline: Facebook's IPO disappoints
text: Facebook, the social network, went public on 18 May at 38 dollars a share, raising 16 billion dollars and valuing it at 104 billion, the highest ever for a newly listed company. Technical problems at Nasdaq delayed trading, and the shares closed the first day at just 38.23. By the end of May they were below 28 dollars.
imageCaption: Mark Zuckerberg, in a hoodie, rings the Nasdaq opening bell from Facebook's headquarters in Menlo Park on the day of the share listing, 18 May 2012
imageCredit: AP Photo / Nasdaq via Facebook, Zef Nikolla

headline: Grexit fears drag down commodities
text: Greece's failure to form a government after the 6 May election revived fears that it could leave the euro; stock markets fell about 6%. Coal, copper and oil all fell: Australian thermal coal averaged $96 a tonne in May, down from $117 in February, and Brent oil $110 from $120. In March Glencore had agreed to buy the Canadian grain handler Viterra for about $6.1bn, whose shareholders approved at the end of May. Xstrata fell 26% in May, and in Peru two people died on 28 May when police broke up protests against alleged pollution at its Tintaya copper mine.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro_area_crisis; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viterra; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/response-to-viterra-shareholder-approval/3137670 (listing title); World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (all read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xstrata
imageCaption: Syntagma Square, 2016

headline: Barrington succeeds Szymanczyk at Altria
text: Martin Barrington became chairman and chief executive of Altria on 17 May, succeeding Michael Szymanczyk, who retired after 23 years with the company, including four as Altria CEO and 12 as head of Philip Morris USA. Altria pays a quarterly dividend of 41 cents a share.

headline: Spain asks Europe to save its banks; half its young people are out of work
text: On 9 June euro finance ministers agreed to lend Spain up to 100 billion euros to recapitalise its banks, which are weighed down by failed mortgages; Bankia, the country's biggest mortgage lender, was nationalised in May and asked for 23.5 billion euros. In June the interest rate on Spain's ten-year bonds reached 7 percent. Almost a quarter of Spaniards, 24.4 percent, were unemployed in March, and among those under 25 the rate is up to 50 percent.
imageCaption: Anti-austerity movement in Spain, 2011

headline: Qatar holds out for a better price
text: Qatar Holding, Xstrata's second-largest shareholder with more than 10%, said on 26 June it would only support the merger at 3.25 Glencore shares per Xstrata share rather than 2.8. Glencore received proposed changes to the contested retention payments for Xstrata managers and will postpone its 11 July shareholder meeting. Ivan Glasenberg says Glencore will not overpay.

headline: Qatar demands more for Xstrata
text: On 26 June Qatar Holding, Xstrata's second-largest shareholder with more than 10%, said it would only back the merger at 3.25 Glencore shares per Xstrata share instead of 2.8; with other dissenting investors it is close to the 16.5% needed to block the deal. Investors are also angry about retention payments of more than £170m for 73 Xstrata executives, and Xstrata's board has proposed changes. Glencore is postponing its shareholder meeting set for 11 July.

headline: Nokia to cut 10,000 jobs
text: On 14 June Nokia said it will cut 10,000 jobs worldwide and close plants, including the Salo factory in Finland, and warned that competition will widen its losses in the second and third quarters. Its shares had already fallen 42% this year. The Finnish government said it will not use an emergency fund to help.
imageCaption: Nokia Lumia 900, 2012

headline: The Model S goes into production
text: Tesla began building and delivering the Model S, its electric luxury saloon, at the Fremont factory in June. Production of the Roadster sports car ended in January. The company is still losing money and must now build cars in volume.
imageCaption: The first Model S deliveries, Fremont, California, 22 June 2012

headline: Federer's seventh Wimbledon
text: Roger Federer beat Andy Murray in the Wimbledon final, his seventh Wimbledon title and 17th Grand Slam title, equalling the records of Pete Sampras and William Renshaw. With the win he is world number one again, at almost 31.

headline: Draghi: whatever it takes
text: Speaking in London on 26 July, the president of the European Central Bank, Mario Draghi, said that within its mandate the ECB 'is ready to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro. And believe me, it will be enough.' Borrowing costs for Spain and Italy, which had climbed to danger levels, fell after the speech.
imageCaption: Mario Draghi, president of the European Central Bank, Davos, January 2012

headline: Don Thompson succeeds Jim Skinner
text: Don Thompson, an engineer who joined McDonald's in 1990 and rose to chief operating officer, became president and chief executive on 1 July, succeeding Jim Skinner, who retired after 41 years. Under Skinner, McDonald's total sales grew from 50.1 billion dollars in 2004 to 70.1 billion in 2008.

headline: Half-year profit dips, shares rebound
text: Glencore's first-half adjusted EBITDA fell 17% to $3.2bn and net income 8% to $2.3bn, as its commodity prices averaged 15% to 28% lower than a year earlier; the trading arm held up better than the mines. Almost all approvals for the Viterra purchase are in, leaving only China. The shares have recovered strongly from their June low.
imageCaption: Ivan Glasenberg, 2013
imageCredit: Financial Times photos c/o: Dianna Bonner

headline: A record stock market value
text: On 20 August Apple's rising shares made it worth a record 624 billion dollars, beating the record set by Microsoft in 1999 (without adjusting for inflation).

headline: QE3: open-ended bond buying
text: On 13 September the Fed said it would buy 40 billion dollars of mortgage bonds a month, with no end date, until the job market improves, and that its rate would likely stay exceptionally low at least through mid-2015. The 10-year Treasury yield averaged 1.5 percent in July, the lowest on record. Gold averaged 1,745 dollars in September, 7 percent more than in August. The numbers: the Fed's rate 0.1 percent. Inflation 1.7 percent. Unemployment 8.1 percent.
imageCaption: The Fed's interest rate (blue), inflation (red) and unemployment (grey) in the United States, 1955 to September 2012
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

headline: Glencore raises to 3.05 and sidelines Davis
text: On the day of the Xstrata vote, 7 September, Glencore asked for more time and on 10 September proposed 3.05 of its shares per Xstrata share, a premium of more than 27% to the trading ratio. The price: Mick Davis would be chief executive of the combined group for only six months before handing over to Ivan Glasenberg. The deal still depends on Xstrata investors approving incentive arrangements for its managers.
imageCaption: Ivan Glasenberg, Glencore's chief executive, speaking at the FT Boldness in Business awards, London

headline: A skydiver breaks the sound barrier, live on YouTube
text: On 14 October the Austrian Felix Baumgartner jumped from a capsule about 39 kilometres above New Mexico, carried up by a helium balloon, and became the first person to break the sound barrier without an engine, reaching about 1,358 kilometres per hour. More than 9.5 million people watched live on YouTube, a record. The project was paid for by Red Bull.

headline: The rial collapses and Tehran's bazaar shuts
text: Iran's currency lost about a third of its value in ten days, falling to around 36,000 rials per dollar on the open market at the start of October. On 3 October riot police broke up the currency market and clashed with money changers, and traders in Tehran's Grand Bazaar closed their shops. Prices of imported food and medicine are soaring. Since July the European Union has bought no Iranian oil, and in March Iranian banks under EU sanctions were cut off from the SWIFT payment network; the International Energy Agency puts Iran's oil exports in September at 860,000 barrels a day, down from 2.2 million at the end of 2011.
imageCaption: Tehran's Grand Bazaar

headline: UBS shrinks its investment bank
text: On 30 October UBS announced it will exit most of its fixed-income trading, keep only advisory, research, equities, currencies and precious metals in the investment bank, and cut costs by another 3.4 billion francs by 2015. The workforce is to fall to about 54,000 from about 64,000. Andrea Orcel takes over the investment bank. UBS aims to pay out 50% or more of profits once its capital plans are met.
imageCaption: Sergio Ermotti, chief executive of UBS

headline: Vikram Pandit out; Michael Corbat takes over
text: Vikram Pandit stepped down as chief executive on 16 October, the day after reporting third-quarter results, and the board elected Michael Corbat to succeed him. Chairman Michael O'Neill praised Pandit for guiding Citigroup through the crisis.
imageCaption: Michael Corbat, Citigroup's chief executive, in New Delhi, April 2015

headline: Disney buys Lucasfilm and Star Wars
text: On 30 October Disney agreed to buy Lucasfilm, George Lucas's company and owner of Star Wars, for 4.05 billion dollars, about half in cash and half in Disney shares. Disney plans new Star Wars films.
imageCaption: Lucasfilm booth at San Diego Comic-Con, 2011 ;;
imageCredit: The Conmunity - Pop Culture Geek from Los Angeles, CA, USA

headline: Windows 8 and the Surface tablet
text: On 26 October Microsoft launched Windows 8, redesigned for touch screens, and the Surface, its own tablet computer.

headline: Obama wins a second term
text: Barack Obama was re-elected on 6 November with 332 electoral votes and 51.1% of the vote against Mitt Romney, holding the swing states of Ohio, Florida, Virginia and Colorado. The campaign was fought over the slow recovery from the financial crisis and Obama's health insurance law, and was the most expensive ever, with new "super PACs" spending freely.

headline: 'Gangnam Style' is the most-watched video ever
text: A song from South Korea has the whole world dancing as if riding an invisible horse. On 24 November 'Gangnam Style' by the singer Psy, released in July, overtook Justin Bieber's 'Baby' as the most-viewed video on YouTube. The song has topped the charts in dozens of countries, and even the Secretary-General of the United Nations, Ban Ki-moon, and the British prime minister have tried the dance.
imageCredit: Korea.net / Korean Culture and Information Service (Jeon Han)

headline: Otellini will retire
text: On 19 November Intel announced that chief executive Paul Otellini will retire in May 2013, after nearly 40 years at the company and eight as chief executive. Intel has failed to win much business in the chips for smartphones and tablets.

headline: Shareholders approve, with Qatar on board
text: Qatar Holding said in mid-November that it would back the revised terms, and on 20 November Xstrata's shareholders approved the merger at 3.05 Glencore shares per Xstrata share. The European Commission cleared the deal on 22 November; antitrust approval from China and a court hearing remain.
source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/xstrata-merger-shareholder-approval/3028319; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Glasenberg (cites Reuters 15 Nov 2012); Investegate GLEN listing 22 Nov 2012 'Merger Update - EU Merger Control Clearance' (all read 2026-10-03)

headline: Gangnam Style passes a billion views
text: On 21 December the video of 'Gangnam Style' by the South Korean singer Psy became the first YouTube video to reach a billion views. Since its release in July its horse-riding dance has spawned parodies and reaction videos around the world.

headline: 2012 in review: up 13 percent, with the fiscal cliff looming
text: The S&P 500 rose 13% in 2012 to 1,426.19 and the Dow 7.3%. As the year ends, Congress has not yet agreed how to avoid the 'fiscal cliff': tax rises and spending cuts that take effect on 1 January and that the Congressional Budget Office says would likely cause a mild recession.

headline: 1.4 billion francs for Libor manipulation
text: On 19 December UBS agreed to pay about 1.4 billion francs in fines and disgorgement to US, UK and Swiss authorities over attempts to manipulate Libor and other benchmark interest rates; its Japanese securities unit pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud. The settlements push UBS to a loss for 2012.
